dish.title: Gochujang Grilled Flank Steak
dish.description: Thin-sliced grilled flank steak in a short gochujang marinade, with a sharp cucumber and scallion salad.

provenance.process: FlavorWeave Catalog Factory Dry Run #1, Grok Bot only

recipe_version.immutability_note: v1 has not been planned, shopped, cooked, or rated. Any material change after that history needs v2. This dry run does not rewrite a prior version.
recipe_version.title: Gochujang Grilled Flank Steak
recipe_version.description: Thin-sliced grilled flank steak in a short gochujang marinade, with a sharp cucumber and scallion salad.

ingredients.name: scallions
ingredients.note: divided: 2 minced into the marinade, 2 sliced for the salad

ingredients.name: kosher salt
ingredients.note: for the salad only; do not salt the steak separately

steps.title: Mix the marinade
steps.body: In a bowl, stir the gochujang, soy sauce, 1 tbsp of the rice vinegar, 3 tsp of the toasted sesame oil, brown sugar, garlic, fresh ginger, and black pepper into a thick paste. Mince 2 of the scallions and stir them in. This marinade cooks on the meat. Do not serve any of it raw.

steps.title: Marinate the steak
steps.body: Pat the flank steak dry and coat both sides with all of the marinade. Leave it at room temperature for 15 minutes. Do not add kosher salt to the steak; the soy sauce is already salty.

steps.title: Make the salad
steps.body: While the steak marinates, thinly slice the cucumber and slice the remaining 2 scallions. Toss them with the remaining 1 tbsp rice vinegar, the remaining 1 tsp toasted sesame oil, the kosher salt, and the sesame seeds.

steps.title: Heat the grill
steps.body: After the 15 minutes, heat a gas or charcoal grill for direct high heat, about 450–500°F. Give it about 10 minutes. When the grates are hot, brush them with the canola oil. This timed method does not overlap preheat with the marinade.

steps.title: Grill
steps.body: Lay the flank steak on the oiled grates. Close the lid on a gas grill, or grill over direct coals with the vents open. Cook 4 to 5 minutes per side. It is done at 130–135°F in the thickest center for medium-rare. Do not press the steak. If the piece is thicker than 1 inch, add about 1 minute per side and trust the thermometer.

steps.title: Rest and slice
steps.body: Move the flank steak to a board and rest it for 5 minutes. Slice it thin, against the grain: cut across the long muscle lines, not parallel to them. Discard any marinade left in the bowl.

steps.title: Plate
steps.body: Serve the slices with the cucumber and scallions beside them. This plate has no rice and no extra sauce.

recipe_version.doneness: 130–135°F in the center for medium-rare, then a 5-minute rest. Slice against the grain.

scaling_notes.1: Buy about 6 oz flank steak, not a tiny scrap that will fall through the grates. Round the marinade down but keep enough to coat: about 2 tsp gochujang, 1 1/2 tsp soy sauce, 3/4 tsp rice vinegar in the marinade and 3/4 tsp in the salad, 3/4 tsp toasted sesame oil in the marinade and 1/4 tsp in the salad, 3/4 tsp brown sugar, 1 garlic clove, 1 tsp grated fresh ginger. Use 1/4 of the cucumber and 1 scallion. Grill temperature stays 450–500°F. A smaller piece of the same thickness may finish about 1 minute sooner per side; use the thermometer.
scaling_notes.2: Halve every quantity. Two garlic cloves is the practical round of 1.5. Grill temperature and target doneness do not change. A half-width steak still needs the 5-minute rest.
scaling_notes.4: As written. 1.5 lb is about 6 oz raw per person.
